summary: Iteration 14 backend testing complete. Tower Talk sales/service dual-mode fully verified. 31/31 new iter14 tests pass covering: (a) mode omitted -> sales default, (b) mode=sales + all 9 sales inquiry types produce non-service-lingo copy, (c) mode=service + all 10 service inquiry types produce advisor-style copy, (d) cross-mode fallback (sales key in service mode -> waiter_status default, service key in sales mode -> new_lead default), (e) unknown inquiry type falls back correctly per mode, (f) case-insensitive mode value (SERVICE), (g) latency < 15s per call, (h) 401 without Bearer, (i) no emoji, no service phrases leaking into sales responses. Full regression across iter10+11+12+13+14 = 119 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures.

NEW cross-mode fallback: mode=sales + inquiryType=waiter_status (service key) -> sales default (new_lead) — 200 OK, no crash ✓
REGRESSION iter10-13: 88 pass + 1 skip (unchanged from iter13 baseline) ✓
REGRESSION sales personality: no emojis, response length reasonable (>20 chars) ✓

PERF: All tower-talk calls completed <15s (well within 5s p50 expectation; 31 tests + 30 param variants ran in ~37s aggregate) ✓
critical_code_review_comments: routes/tower_talk_v2.py: mode routing is clean — single is_service_mode boolean, guidance_dict swap, fallback_key swap, and one if/else on system_message. Minimal surface area, low regression risk.
TowerTalkRequest.mode is Optional[str] with default 'sales' — proper backward compat.
Case-normalization uses .lower() on the mode string — verified 'SERVICE' works.
SERVICE_INQUIRY_GUIDANCE dict has all 10 keys matching mobile serviceInquiries.ts presets (spot-checked waiter_status, comeback, warranty_claim, schedule_appointment).
Service-mode system prompt keeps the same non-negotiable rules (2-3 sentences, no emojis, no brackets, signed-off if salesperson provided) — parity with sales-mode prompt.
Emoji strip (_strip_emoji) applies uniformly to both modes — no regression path.

Minor observation: guidance_dict[fallback_key] is looked up unconditionally after .get() — safe because both fallback keys ('new_lead' and 'waiter_status') are guaranteed to exist in their respective dicts. Defensive but acceptable.

success_rate.backend: 100% (31/31 new + 88/89 regression, 1 pre-existing skip); 119/120 executed = 99.2% incl. skip
